text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele presents the draft of his government declaration to potential members of the ruling coalition. Parliament factions have until Friday to submit their proposals to the document. Parliament's vote on backing Shkele is likely to happen by February 13. The main items of Shkele's programme are the reform of local governments, streamlining the medical care funding system and the privatisation of 20 percent of apartments by the end of 1997.
- Shkele starts talks with Democratic Party Saimnieks and Latvia's Way to form the new cabinet. Saimnieks has put forward candidates for all posts, leaving the choice to Shkele.
- The father of triplets born recently in Riga, turned out to be a petty thief with four previous convictions. He was rearrested after his photo appeared in the press.
- Customs seized more than seven million cigarettes worth about three million lats.
- The ministry of education signed a loan agreement with the World Bank to receive $20-30 million for an education development programme.
- Riga city council votes against the destruction of the Liberation Monument, a huge Soviet-era monument to Red Army troops.
- The ferry boat Russ, which was suspended from servicing the Riga-Stockholm route by Swedish authorities, has finally received a temporary certificate.
- British Airways will start flights between Riga and London from March 30.
- The volume of transit cargoes passing through Latvian ports increased by 20.7 percent to 44.8 million tonnes. Of all transit cargoes, 93 percent were from East to West.
- The Bank of Latvia cut the 31-day deposit rate for banks to 3.5 percent from 4.5 percent.
